subject.title: [Bug]: 2 codex accounts, same machine, same docs, one has balloon startup cost

question: Should local Codex app-server CODEX_HOME remain per-agent, or should OpenClaw make it per-auth-profile for OAuth-backed runs and define an upgrade/reset path?
rationale: The source path supports account-scoped isolation as the likely fix, but changing CODEX_HOME affects existing Codex auth, sessions, plugins, logs, and state cleanup, so automation should not choose the product/upgrade behavior alone.

options.title: Account-scope with upgrade plan
options.body: Make Codex app-server homes auth-profile-scoped, document where state moves, and choose either migration or explicit reset/cleanup for existing per-agent state.

options.title: Keep per-agent storage and add recovery
options.body: Leave the current storage boundary intact but add diagnostics or a reset command that helps users clear contaminated Codex state without moving the default path.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides redacted two-account proof that isolates the cached-prefix cause from upstream account-specific Codex behavior.

recommendation.title: Account-scope with upgrade plan
recommendation.body: Make Codex app-server homes auth-profile-scoped, document where state moves, and choose either migration or explicit reset/cleanup for existing per-agent state.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is connected to landing related Codex OAuth runtime work and is the strongest available routing candidate for the upgrade/product decision.
